subject: Art & Design
title: Art Nouveau: Nature Meets Architecture
description: A quick, practical guide to Art Nouveau: Nature Meets Architecture.

hook.text: Gaudí's Casa Batlló in Barcelona has no straight lines. It looks alive — bones, scales, a dragon's spine.

buildup.text: Art Nouveau (1890–1910) rejected industrial-age straight lines in favor of organic curves from nature.

discovery.text: Whiplash curves, floral motifs, stained glass, and ironwork defined the style. Every surface was decorated.

twist.text: The movement lasted only 20 years. Its handcrafted approach was too expensive for an industrializing world.

climax.text: Paris Métro entrances by Hector Guimard remain the style's most visible legacy — seen by millions daily.

punchline.text: Art Nouveau was a love letter to nature, written in iron and glass.

quiz.question: Why did Art Nouveau decline after only about 20 years?
options: Its handcrafted approach was too expensive for industrial-age mass production

details.summary: Art Nouveau (1890-1910) rejected industrial straight lines in favor of organic curves inspired by plants, flowers, and insects. Architects like Gaudí, Horta, and Guimard designed buildings where structure and decoration merged — iron columns became flower stems, doorways became butterfly wings.
details.whyItMatters: Art Nouveau was the first modern style to unify architecture with decorative arts. It demonstrated that ornamentation could be structural and that nature offered an alternative to historical imitation.
takeaways: Rejected industrial geometry for organic curves from nature
Structure and decoration merged into unified organic forms
Gaudí, Horta, and Guimard were leading practitioners

faq.question: What makes Art Nouveau different from other styles?
faq.answer: Art Nouveau rejected both industrial aesthetics and historical revival styles. Instead, it drew from nature — whiplash curves, floral motifs, and insect forms. Every detail from doorknobs to roof tiles was designed as part of a single organic vision.

faq.question: Why did Art Nouveau last only about 20 years?
faq.answer: Its elaborate handcrafted decoration was extremely expensive to produce. As modernism emerged with its industrial materials and stripped-down aesthetic, Art Nouveau was criticized as excessive. World War I ended the era's optimism that had fueled its exuberance.
